tasks.title: an untouched prefill no longer overwrites another admin's record entry
tasks.redPrompt:
Write the FAILING suite for #280. Contract = `cd ~/workspace-app && gh issue view 280 --comments`. Research = `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-280-244.json` (issue280 section). Drift-check every line — #287 (`859f6a4`) and #294 (`c2829ea`) both landed in `roster/+page.svelte` after this issue was written.

## The defect, precisely
`openRecordEditor` prefills `name` (from `row.profileName ?? row.name`) and `email` (from `row.email`) when the save-time lookup state is `'none'`, and sets `recordEditorOriginal = null`. `recordEditorOriginal` is populated ONLY on the `state === 'one'` branch. So on the create-turned-update path — editor opened while no record existed, but a fresh save-time re-read finds one — the baseline falls back to all-empty strings, the diff computes `recordForm.name !== ''` and `recordForm.email !== ''` as CHANGED, and both untouched prefilled values are sent, silently overwriting whatever the other writer saved.

**Only `name` and `email` are affected.** `phone`, `birthdate` and `id_code` open blank, so they never differ from the empty baseline and are already correctly omitted. Do not widen the pins beyond the two prefilled fields.

## AN EXISTING TEST ENCODES THE BUG — this is the most important thing in this brief
`src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:943-968` is #268's create-turned-update test. It asserts `updateMemberRecordMock.mock.calls[0][2]` **toEqual `{ name: 'Berta Bass', email: 'berta@example.com' }`** — i.e. it currently REQUIRES the untouched prefilled fields be sent, and its comment states the guarantee the PO has since overturned.

**That expectation must be REWRITTEN as part of this work**, not worked around and not deleted wholesale. The scenario it drives is exactly right and must survive; only the assertion changes — an untouched-prefill save on that path now sends `{}`. Rewrite it in place, keep its comment honest about why it changed, and cite #280.

## Pins
1. **Untouched prefill is not sent.** Open the editor with no record (prefill fires on name+email), touch nothing, make the save-time re-read return an existing record → `updateMemberRecord` is called with `{}`. The other writer's values survive.
2. **A typed field IS sent and wins.** Same setup, but type into `name` → only `name` is sent; `email` (still untouched prefill) is not.
3. **Editing then reverting.** Type into `name`, then restore it to exactly the prefilled value. Decide and pin the intended behaviour explicitly rather than leaving it to the implementation — state your choice and its reasoning in the result summary.
4. **The normal update path is unchanged.** Editor opened when a record already existed (`recordEditorOriginal` is a real baseline) — the existing spec at :546-559 asserts only the genuinely-changed field is sent, and must stay green untouched.
5. **The blank fields stay omitted.** `phone`/`birthdate`/`id_code` untouched → still absent from `changes`.

## Do not chase these
- **The write layer is fine.** `updateMemberRecord` (`src/lib/roster/memberRecord.ts:216-262`) walks `FIELD_ORDER` and skips any field not present as a key (`if (!(field in changes)) continue;`), delegating to `replaceEntityProperty` per named property. **A field omitted from `changes` is never sent and is left untouched server-side — omission cannot clear anything.** Verified from source and unit-confirmed at `memberRecord.spec.ts:214-231`. So 'don't send it' is sufficient; do not add clearing logic or a sentinel.
- **Do not refuse the save.** The PO explicitly withdrew that: the likeliest reason a record exists at save time is the admin's own retry after an ambiguous create failure, and refusing strands them on their own action.

tasks.commitBody: An untouched prefill is a display of the profile, not an assertion about the record, and it no longer wins a write against a value someone typed. On the create-turned-update path — editor opened when no record existed, a fresh save-time read finding one — the diff baseline fell back to empty strings, so the `name` and `email` that #265 prefills counted as changed despite the admin never touching them, and they overwrote whatever another admin had already saved. The loss was narrow and silent: those two fields only, untouched only, two overlapping writers only, on real admin-entered data. The write layer was never at fault — it already omits any field absent from the diff, and omission cannot clear a value — so the fix is entirely in knowing which fields the saver actually asserted. #268's create-turned-update test asserted the old behaviour, with a comment stating a guarantee that holds for empty fields but not for prefilled ones; its scenario is kept and its expectation corrected rather than removed. ## THE ISSUE'S IDENTIFIERS NO LONGER EXIST — do not search for them
#261 (`b58d334`) removed the gear entirely. `season-manage-gear` and `seasonManageGearDisabled` are GONE. Successors, verified at HEAD in `src/routes/+page.svelte`:
- panel state: `seasonManageOpen` (~:2481)
- collapsed face opens it: `season-card-expand` (~:5704) → `openSeasonManagePanel()` (~:2862)
- opened face collapses it: `season-card-collapse` (~:5763) → `closeSeasonManagePanel()` (~:2936), gated by `seasonCardCollapseDisabled` (~:4710)
- refusal condition: `seasonCardCollapseDisabled = seasonManageOpen && (seriesRunUnfinished || eventConvertRunUnfinished)`

## The amended behaviour — three conditions on the collapse
1. **Only on SUCCESS.** Every failure branch in `submitEventCreate` (~:4305-4454) sets an error and returns with the panel and form intact. Pin that a failed create does NOT collapse — collapsing would hide the error.
2. **Only when the agenda can actually show the new event.** THE AMENDMENT: if the active type filter excludes the created event's type, the panel STAYS OPEN and nothing else changes. The collapse's whole justification is uncovering the result; with no result to uncover the premise fails. Pin both directions — collapses when the filter admits the type, does not when it excludes it.
3. **Never mid-run.** `seasonCardCollapseDisabled`'s condition must be respected. Routing the auto-collapse through `closeSeasonManagePanel()` gets this for free since that function re-checks `seriesRunUnfinished || eventConvertRunUnfinished` itself (~:2958). Pin that a create succeeding while a bulk series/conversion run is unfinished does NOT tear down the panel showing that run's progress.

## NO FILTER WRITE — pin it as an absence
`agendaTypeFilter` (~:220) is user-set state. The app must not write it on this path, in either case. The three existing writes to it (~:277, :652, :714, plus the auto-reset effect) are legitimate resets on a collective switch / no-agenda / vanishing chip — none narrows the filter to fit a new event, and this path must not become the first. Assert no write occurs.

## Surface the row: scroll + transient mark
- Rows live in `src/lib/components/agenda/AgendaList.svelte`, testid `agenda-row-{item.id}` (~:543) and `agenda-recent-row-{item.id}` (~:396), keyed by the event entity id. `+page.svelte` already addresses rows cross-component by that selector (~:1957) — no new prop or element ref needed.
- **`createEvent`'s return value is currently DISCARDED** at ~:4415. It resolves to the new event's entity id (`src/lib/entity/entityCreate.ts:492`). Capture it — without the id there is no row to target and no type to check the filter against.
- **No transient-highlight pattern exists anywhere in this codebase.** Nearest analogs: a STATIC `class:bg-highlight={group.relative === 'today'}` (AgendaList ~:515, never times out) and the scroll pattern in `AttendanceSurface.svelte:89-97` (`tick().then(() => el?.scrollIntoView(...))`). So the mark is genuinely new — build it small, and pin its appearance AND its clearing, since a highlight that never clears is a different bug.

## Focus — resolve a real collision deliberately
Today `restoreEventCreateFocus(origin)` (~:3437) focuses `seasonManagePanelEl` on success. `closeSeasonManagePanel()` unconditionally focuses `seasonManageExpandEl` (~:2978). If the auto-collapse routes through it, BOTH fire on the same microtask queue and ordering decides which wins. Pin a single deliberate outcome — never `<body>` — and pin it separately for the collapsed and stayed-open cases.

## i18n
New copy needs all four bundles (`messages/{en,et,lv,uk}.json`), keys snake_case `<domain>_<subject>[_<detail>]` matching neighbours (`event_created`, `agenda_filter_*`). Keys stay vocabulary-neutral.

## Out of scope — do not build
A VISIBLE create confirmation. `event-create-status` (~:7239) is `sr-only` and that gap is **#298**, filed separately and not `ready`. The amendment exists precisely so this issue does not need one.

tasks.commitBody: After a successful event create, the season panel gets out of the way and the new event is surfaced where the user is looking — but only when there is something to surface. The panel collapses on success, scrolls the created event's agenda row into view and marks it transiently; if the active type filter excludes that event, the panel stays open instead and nothing else changes, because the collapse's only justification is uncovering the result and there is no result to uncover. Collapsing there would have removed the last thing on screen, which is worse than today. No filter chip is ever written: the chips are state the user set on purpose, and moving them on the app's initiative would mean a later reading of them no longer reflects a choice anyone made. The collapse routes through the existing close handler so an unfinished bulk series or conversion run still refuses it, rather than tearing down the panel showing that run's progress. The visible-confirmation gap this surfaced — a successful create is announced only to screen readers — is #298, deliberately not solved here.
